title: The Dwarves: Big Box - Review
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1GeNGNh50Fw

Daniel (@dungeondive) went looking on Amazon for a fantasy adventure game he could simply buy — no crowdfunder, no hoops, no waiting — and came back with Pegasus Spiele's *The Dwarves: Big Box*, around $55 and based on a novel series by Markus Heitz he knew nothing about. It is not a top ten game, he says, but it packs a great deal into a normal-sized box.

The shape will be familiar to anyone who has played *Legends of Andor* or *Defenders of the Realm*: cooperative threat management, simpler than either, and the simplicity is what he admires. Five books' worth of saga cards give you scenarios you can play in any order; orcs, trolls and Alfar spawn at numbered gates and march on Black Saddle, corrupting hexes as they go. Everything resolves on a d6 pool — four, five or six to hit, depending on what you are swinging at — with almost no way to mitigate a cold streak until gear arrives.

The standout is the dwarven council track, a political tug-of-war humming away beneath the quests, handing out bonuses or penalties as the party's standing shifts. The complaints are all component-level: the meeples are too tall, too easy to knock over, and they bury the hex names a fast game needs you to find quickly. He would replace them with cubes.

----

Would swapping the meeples for cubes fix this game for you, or do you want the toys on the table regardless?
